# ADR-001: Keep Redis as the default cart store; Spanner and AlloyDB as opt-in backends

Status: accepted · Decided: 2022-10-02 · Synthetic ADR written for the Blastradius demo, grounded in real PRs: #1109, #1578.

## Context
cartservice stores carts in an in-cluster Redis (redis-cart). Platform teams demoing Online Boutique on Google Cloud asked to show managed databases, but the default install must stay self-contained and free.

## Decision
Redis stays the default cart store. Spanner (#1109 "`cartservice` - Spanner as database option") and AlloyDB (#1578 "Add AlloyDB as a Kustomize backend option") are optional backends selected by environment variables and shipped as Kustomize components, not in the default manifests.

## Consequences
cartservice carries three store implementations and must pick exactly one at startup (see INC-2023-004). The default install needs no cloud account. Each backend needs its own docs and tests.

## Pull requests
- #1109 `cartservice` - Spanner as database option (Daniel Quinlan)
- #1578 Add AlloyDB as a Kustomize backend option (Gabe Weiss)
props.title: ADR-001: Keep Redis as the default cart store; Spanner and AlloyDB as opt-in backends

props.text:
# ADR-002: Use native Kubernetes gRPC probes instead of the grpc-health-probe binary

Status: accepted · Decided: 2022-10-12 · Synthetic ADR written for the Blastradius demo, grounded in real PRs: #1102, #1837, #1840.

## Context
Every gRPC service image bundled the grpc-health-probe binary just for liveness and readiness checks, which added CVE noise and image size. Kubernetes 1.24+ supports gRPC probes natively.

## Decision
Offer a Kustomize variation without the binary (#1102 "Kustomize variation to deploy Online Boutique apps without the `grpc-health-probe` bin"), then remove it everywhere (#1837 "Remove use of gRPC health probe binary") and from the Helm chart (#1840 "Remove `nativeGrpcHealthCheck` from Helm chart").

## Consequences
Smaller images, fewer CVEs; requires Kubernetes 1.24+. Probe timings must be tuned per service: the JVM adservice needs a longer start (INC-2023-008).

## Pull requests
- #1102 Kustomize variation to deploy Online Boutique apps without the `grpc-health-probe` bin (Mathieu Benoit)
- #1837 Remove use of gRPC health probe binary (Nim Jayawardena)
- #1840 Remove `nativeGrpcHealthCheck` from Helm chart (Mathieu Benoit)
props.title: ADR-002: Use native Kubernetes gRPC probes instead of the grpc-health-probe binary

# ADR-003: Ship minimal container base images (digest-pinned, scratch for Go)

Status: accepted · Decided: 2022-11-25 · Synthetic ADR written for the Blastradius demo, grounded in real PRs: #1312, #2512.

## Context
Base images were pulled by tag and carried shells and package managers we never use, so vulnerability scanners flagged every release.

## Decision
Pin base images by digest (#1312 "Use `digest` instead of `tag` for container base images") and build the Go services checkout, frontend, productcatalog and shipping FROM scratch (#2512 "`scratch` for `checkout`, `frontend`, `productcatalog` and `shipping`").

## Consequences
Much smaller attack surface; no shell for debugging (use ephemeral debug containers). Anything the binary needs at runtime (CA certificates, timezone data) must be copied in explicitly.

## Pull requests
- #1312 Use `digest` instead of `tag` for container base images (Mathieu Benoit)
- #2512 `scratch` for `checkout`, `frontend`, `productcatalog` and `shipping` (Mathieu Benoit)
props.title: ADR-003: Ship minimal container base images (digest-pinned, scratch for Go)

# ADR-004: Add a Gemini shopping assistant backed by an AlloyDB vector store

Status: accepted · Decided: 2024-04-06 · Synthetic ADR written for the Blastradius demo, grounded in real PRs: #2466, #2490.

## Context
We wanted a generative-AI feature in the demo that recommends products from a photo of a room, using retrieval over the real catalogue.

## Decision
Build shoppingassistantservice in Python with LangChain: Gemini for generation, AlloyDB for PostgreSQL with pgvector for product embeddings (#2466 "Add ShoppingAssistant, and AlloyDB support to ProductCatalog"). It is an optional Kustomize component; dependencies are refreshed regularly (#2490 "Bump shoppingassistant deps").

## Consequences
The assistant needs a Google API key and an AlloyDB instance, so it is off by default. Connection pooling to AlloyDB matters (INC-2024-005).

## Pull requests
- #2466 Add ShoppingAssistant, and AlloyDB support to ProductCatalog (Olivier Bourgeois)
- #2490 Bump shoppingassistant deps (Olivier Bourgeois)
props.title: ADR-004: Add a Gemini shopping assistant backed by an AlloyDB vector store

# ADR-005: Route traces and metrics through an OpenTelemetry Collector

Status: accepted · Decided: 2022-10-26 · Synthetic ADR written for the Blastradius demo, grounded in real PRs: #1167, #1180.

## Context
Services exported directly to Cloud Trace with vendor libraries, so tracing only worked on Google Cloud.

## Decision
Add an OpenTelemetry Collector (#1167 "feat!: Add OpenTelemetry Collector") and instrument the services with OpenTelemetry for distributed tracing (#1180 "feat!: Add distributed tracing to Online Boutique").

## Consequences
Vendor-neutral telemetry; one more component to run. Services must propagate trace context on every call.

## Pull requests
- #1167 feat!: Add OpenTelemetry Collector (Drew Brown)
- #1180 feat!: Add distributed tracing to Online Boutique (Drew Brown)
props.title: ADR-005: Route traces and metrics through an OpenTelemetry Collector

# ADR-006: Turn off Cloud Profiler in adservice by default

Status: accepted · Decided: 2024-04-29 · Synthetic ADR written for the Blastradius demo, grounded in real PRs: #2518.

## Context
The Cloud Profiler agent in adservice failed outside Google Cloud and added startup time to an already slow JVM service.

## Decision
Comment out the profiler agent in the adservice image (#2518 "Comment out profiler in adservice"); re-enable it per environment when needed.

## Consequences
Faster, more portable adservice startup; no continuous profiling by default.

## Pull requests
- #2518 Comment out profiler in adservice (Olivier Bourgeois)
props.title: ADR-006: Turn off Cloud Profiler in adservice by default

# ADR-007: Move cartservice to .NET 8

Status: accepted · Decided: 2023-09-05 · Synthetic ADR written for the Blastradius demo, grounded in real PRs: #2102, #2264.

## Context
.NET 7 support ended in May 2024; .NET 8 is the long-term support release.

## Decision
Upgrade cartservice to .NET 8 previews (#2102 "`cartservice` - .NET 8") and to the GA release (#2264 "`cartservice` - .NET 8 is out").

## Consequences
LTS runtime; container defaults changed (the default HTTP port is now 8080, see INC-2023-014).

## Pull requests
- #2102 `cartservice` - .NET 8 (Mathieu Benoit)
- #2264 `cartservice` - .NET 8 is out (Mathieu Benoit)

props.rootCause: Backend selection checked for the presence of the AlloyDB variable rather than a non-empty value, so an empty string selected AlloyDB.
props.summary: #1578 "Add AlloyDB as a Kustomize backend option" added AlloyDB as a cart backend. On clusters where the ALLOYDB_PRIMARY_IP variable was left empty in a shared ConfigMap, cartservice tried the AlloyDB code path instead of redis-cart and failed AddItem/GetCart for 40 minutes.
props.title: cartservice ignored redis-cart after AlloyDB backend option

props.rootCause: The new opentelemetry-instrumentation-grpc pin required a newer grpcio than requirements.txt allowed; pip resolved an incompatible pair at image build time.
props.summary: After #1803 "Bump opentel to 1.18.0", emailservice failed on import and crash-looped. checkout's order confirmation calls failed (orders still placed) for 55 minutes.
props.title: emailservice crash-loop after OpenTelemetry 1.18 bump

props.rootCause: The native readinessProbe/livenessProbe on port 9555 kept the old 15s initial delay; the Java service needs ~40s on small nodes, so the liveness probe restarted it in a loop.
props.summary: #1837 "Remove use of gRPC health probe binary" replaced the grpc-health-probe binary with native Kubernetes gRPC probes. adservice's JVM took longer to start than the probe's initial delay, so pods were killed before becoming ready and the storefront showed no ads for an hour.
props.title: adservice never became ready after switching to native gRPC probes

props.rootCause: The new grpc-go version enforced keepalive pings more strictly; checkout's client keepalive was more aggressive than the Node payment server allowed, so connections were closed with GOAWAY under load.
props.summary: After #1945 "fix(deps): update module google.golang.org/grpc to v1.56.2" bumped google.golang.org/grpc in the Go services, checkout's calls to paymentservice timed out for 6% of orders over 45 minutes.
props.title: checkout → payment DEADLINE_EXCEEDED after grpc-go bump

props.rootCause: The new unmarshalling rejected an unknown field in products.json and the error path returned an empty catalogue instead of failing the readiness probe.
props.summary: #2013 "Fix deprecated methods in productcatalog" replaced deprecated protobuf/JSON methods in productcatalogservice. A parsing difference made products.json load as an empty list on one replica set; the home page showed no products and recommendations failed for 35 minutes.
props.title: productcatalogservice returned an empty catalogue after protobuf API cleanup

props.rootCause: .NET 8 container images set ASPNETCORE_HTTP_PORTS=8080 by default, which overrode the Kestrel port the service used to bind.
props.summary: After #2102 "`cartservice` - .NET 8" moved cartservice to .NET 8, new pods listened on port 8080. frontend and checkout could not reach cartservice:7070; the shop was unusable for 25 minutes until rollback.
props.title: cartservice stopped listening on 7070 after .NET 8 upgrade

props.rootCause: pino was configured with a synchronous destination and info-level logging of each request.
props.summary: #2263 "Use pino instead of console.log" replaced console.log with pino in currency and payment. currencyservice, the highest-QPS service, logged every conversion synchronously and p99 rose from 8 ms to 35 ms; storefront pages slowed.
props.title: currencyservice p99 latency up 4x after switching to pino

props.rootCause: The zip code rule only accepted digits; the loadgenerator only sent US-style codes, so tests passed.
props.summary: #2438 "feat: Implement validation for HTTP FormValue(s) in frontend microser…" added server-side validation for form values in frontend. Postal codes with letters and some country names failed validation, and 18% of checkout attempts got HTTP 422 for two hours.

props.rootCause: Each request created a new AlloyDBEngine connection for the vector store instead of reusing a pooled engine; idle connections were not released fast enough.
props.summary: A week after #2466 "Add ShoppingAssistant, and AlloyDB support to ProductCatalog" launched the ShoppingAssistant, a traffic spike exhausted its AlloyDB connection pool. /assistant requests from the frontend returned 504 for 50 minutes.
props.title: shopping assistant timeouts: AlloyDB connection pool exhausted

props.text:
Nim Jayawardena: Why does cartservice have Spanner and AlloyDB stores at all? Redis is the default and that's what everyone runs.
Mathieu Benoit: Because people demo Online Boutique on Google Cloud and want to show managed databases. Daniel Quinlan added Spanner in #1109, Gabe Weiss added AlloyDB in #1578.
Mathieu Benoit: But the default install must stay self-contained, so Redis (redis-cart) stays the default and the other stores are opt-in Kustomize components. It's ADR-001.
Nim Jayawardena: Got it: Spanner and AlloyDB are optional cart backends; Redis is the default cart store.
props.title: Why does cartservice support Spanner and AlloyDB if Redis is the default?

props.text:
Mathieu Benoit: Who knows the shopping assistant? And why does it need AlloyDB instead of the products.json the catalog uses?
Olivier Bourgeois: That's me, I built it in #2466. It does retrieval: product descriptions are embedded and stored in AlloyDB with pgvector, then Gemini answers using the closest products.
Olivier Bourgeois: products.json has no vector search, so the assistant needs a vector store; AlloyDB was the managed option. Written up in ADR-004.
Mathieu Benoit: Thanks. So the assistant needs AlloyDB for vector search and is off by default.
props.title: Who knows the shopping assistant, and why does it need AlloyDB?

Mathieu Benoit: kubectl debug with an ephemeral container. The smaller attack surface is worth it; see ADR-003.
Olivier Bourgeois: OK, but let's double-check CA certificates are copied in, or outbound TLS breaks.
